2. The relevant that giving rise to this Rule, in short, is that the opposite-party No. 1 as plaintiff instituted a suit for declaration of title and partition contending, inter-alia, that Bhayrab Chandra Gaop, Ghushal Gaop and Ramjoy Gaop got the suit by way of Tartan' but the concerned C.S. Khatian was recorded erroneously in the name of Bhayrab Chandra Gaop and Ram Joy Gaop omitting the name of Ghushal Gaop, although in the suit Ghushal Gaop, Bahyrab Chandra Gaop and Ram Joy Gaop owned the suit in equal shares. Ghushal Gaop died leaving behind Brindabon Gaop to inherit 1/3 share of the suit jote and Brindabon sold 121/2 decimals of suit land to plaintiff's father. The defendant No. 1 being the sole legal heir of Bhairab Chandra, he became owner 1/3 of suit jote and plaintiff has been residing in northern portion of suit dag 509 by constructing house and possessing 71/2 decimals of suit dag 513 but R.S. Khatian erroneously, shows 1/3 to the plaintiff and 2/3 to the defendants' father. The defendant raised objection regarding the plaintiff's right, title and interest aver the suit land and hence the instant suit. 

 3. The defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing written statements denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter-alia, that Bhairab Chandra Goap being the owner of 16 decimals of plot No. 509 and 6 decimals of plot No. 513 died leaving Ninth Kari Gaon who died leaving Shachindra to inherit the said land. Shachindra died leaving behind the defendant No.1 who has been owning and possessing 16 decimals land of plot No. 513 by mutating his name and paying rents to the authority concerned. B.S. Khatian was rightly recorded in the name of the predecessors of the plaintiff and defendant to their respective portion and Brindabon Goap did not have any title and possession over the suit land and that being the position the plaintiff cannot have legally any title and interest over the suit land by virtue of alleged deed dated 05.11.1925 and the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 11. On perusal of the record it appears that the plaintiff brought a suit for declaration of title and partition claiming 651/4 acres of land by inheritance and purchase. In support of the claim the plaintiff examined 4 witnesses and exhibited their documents marked as exhibit-1 deed No. 5649 dated 05.11.1925, exhibits-2 C.S. khatian No. 841, exhibits- 2(ka) S.A. khatian No. 863, exhibits-2(Kha) R.S. khatian No. 1422, exhibits-3 D.C.R., exhibits- 3(ka) and 3(kha) 02 rent receipts. The defendant also examined 04(four) witnesses and exhibited their documents marked as exhibits `ka' D.C.R., exhibits- (ka-1) rent receipt.
